subject: maths

subject: maths
prompt_en: Meena says: 'The train goes 1,384 km. I rounded it to 1,400 km, so now the train runs 16 km extra.' What would you tell her?

subject: maths
prompt_en: A line goes from 0 to 2 and each whole is split into 4 equal parts. Where is 5/4?
prompt_hi: Ek line 0 se 2 tak hai aur har poora hissa 4 barabar parts mein bata hai. 5/4 kahaan hai?
answer: The first mark after 1 (one quarter past 1)

subject: maths
prompt_en: On a 0-to-1 line split into 3 equal parts, one of 1/3 and 2/3 is before the middle and one is after. Which is which, and why?
prompt_hi: 0 se 1 ki line 3 barabar parts mein bati hai. 1/3 aur 2/3 mein se ek beech se pehle hai aur ek baad mein. Kaun kahaan, aur kyun?
answer: 1/3 is before the middle and 2/3 is after, because the middle is 1/2 and 1/3 < 1/2 < 2/3

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why do we count the gaps, not the marks, to name a fraction on the number line?
prompt_hi: Number line par fraction ka naam dene ke liye hum gaps kyun ginte hain, marks kyun nahi?
answer: A fraction is a length from 0, and each equal gap is one part; 3 marks between 0 and 1 make 4 gaps, so each gap is 1/4

subject: maths
prompt_en: Tinku split 0 to 1 with 4 marks in between and called the first mark 1/4. Check his work.
prompt_hi: Tinku ne 0 se 1 ke beech 4 marks lagaaye aur pehle mark ko 1/4 kaha. Uska kaam check karo.
